newsitem.title: UK: Peptide in BTG licensing agreeement.
newsitem.headline: Peptide in BTG licensing agreeement.

text.p: Peptide Therapeutics Group Plc said on Monday it had signed an "exlusive worldwide licensing agreement with BTG Plc for the development of an innovative allergy vaccine for use in the veterinary field".
The Cambridge-based biotechnology company said the allergy vaccine had "the potential to protect against a wide range of allergies irrespective of the causative agent".
Peptide said current methods for treating animal allergies are difficult and costly and can involve special diets and treatment with steroids.
The company said it was in discussions with "major U.S. and European multinationals to collaborate in commercialising the relevant animal peptide sequence based vaccine for use in companion animals".
It said BTG had already licensed the vaccine technology to it for use in the human allergy field.
BTG shares were up 75p at 2462.5 pence at 0918 GMT while Peptide's shares were up 8.5p at 203.5 pence at 0914 GMT.

Peter Bailey, director of BTG's Biosciences Division, said Peptide Therapeutic's work on human allergy vaccine was progressing well and the company was "well placed to establish a strategic alliance which would lead to commercialising the vaccine for uses in the veterinary field".
Peptide's chairman Brian Richards said the licence agreement was a "logical extension" to its allergy product portfolio.
"I am confident we will rapidly identify a suitable partner to complete the development and fully exploit what is one of the largest unmet needs in the veterinary vaccine field," he said.
